rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – good cause required to evict or not renew
rules.requirement: Residential landlords may not evict or refuse to renew a lease, written or oral, without one of the statutory good causes in N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)-(r). The causes include nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule or lease violations, refusal of a reasonable rent increase or lease change, habitual late payment, health and safety or illegal occupancy, permanent retirement from residential use, condo conversion, owner or buyer occupancy in buildings of 3 or fewer units, termination of employment-based tenancy, and certain criminal convictions. Each cause has a required notice to quit, ranging from 3 days to 3 years: 1 month for rule or lease breaches and rent increases, 3 months for health and safety or removal from the rental market, 18 months for retirement from residential use, 3 years for condo conversion, and 2 months for owner or buyer occupancy. Tenants evicted for illegal occupancy get relocation assistance equal to 6 times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord. A landlord who recovers a unit for personal occupancy must occupy it for 6 months; a property retired from residential use may not be used residentially for 5 years.
rules.key_value: Good cause required for eviction or non-renewal; notice to quit 3 days to 3 years depending on cause; relocation assistance of 6x monthly rent for illegal-occupancy evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including apartment buildings, single-family homes, mobile homes and rooming houses. Excludes owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units: tenants there can be removed after lease expiration on 3-month or 1-month notice under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a). Hotel, motel and guest-house transient or seasonal guests, unless the occupant has no alternate residence. Units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.interaction: Rent-increase evictions under 2A:18-61.1(f) also require compliance with any municipal rent control ordinance.

rules.penalty: For violating owner-occupancy or retirement/demolition re-use limits: treble damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.6).

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – rent increases must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: No statewide numeric cap exists. A landlord may raise rent only by terminating the lease with proper written notice to quit and notice of rent increase, effective at the end of the lease term. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal rent control ordinance. Courts decide whether an increase is unconscionable on the facts, considering the size of the increase, the landlord's expenses and profitability, comparable rents, and bargaining position. Tenants can be evicted for nonpayment only of a lawful, non-unconscionable increase.
rules.key_value: No numeric cap; increase must not be unconscionable; no mid-lease increases
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Anti-Eviction Act (excludes owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units).
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient or seasonal hotel and motel units.
rules.interaction: Applies alongside municipal rent control or rent leveling ordinances; the increase must also comply with the local ordinance.

rules.title: Security Deposit Law – cap, interest, notices and 30-day return
rules.requirement: The security deposit may not exceed 1.5 times one month's rent, and any yearly increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid or last month's rent and any pet deposit count toward the cap, so no more than 2.5 months' rent may be collected at lease inception, including first month's rent. Deposits must be held in trust in an interest-bearing account at a New Jersey institution, with interest belonging to the tenant and paid annually or credited to rent. The landlord must give written notice of the bank, amount, account type and interest rate within 30 days of receipt and annually. If notice or interest is not provided, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% interest to rent. The deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, must be returned within 30 days after termination by personal delivery, registered or certified mail. It must be returned within 5 business days if the tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. A new owner is responsible for the deposit.
rules.key_value: Max 1.5x monthly rent; return within 30 days with interest and itemized deductions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. Excludes owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the law applicable by written request (effective 30 days later). Seasonal rentals of 125 days or less are exempt from the investment and interest provisions.
rules.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1). Civil penalty of $500-$2,000 per offense for willfully withholding deposits of assisted tenants (N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.5). Disorderly persons offense for unlawful use of deposit monies: fine of at least $200 and/or up to 30 days imprisonment (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).

rules.title: Law Against Discrimination – source of lawful income and other protected classes in rental
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rental based on race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.key_value: Source of lawful income is a protected class in rental screening
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships, with narrow owner-occupancy exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; single-sex residences; age-restricted housing (as to familial status).
rules.quoted_span: nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.penalty: Monetary damages; fines up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a).

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no statewide rent control or rent cap law. Municipalities may adopt their own rent control or rent leveling ordinances.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents.
